title: Expressions, Functions, count, for_each and Dynamic Blocks

header.html: 4e Write dynamic configuration using expressions and functions
the official Terraform Associate (004) exam content list

html:
1Expressions

An expression computes a value inside configuration.

Expression Example Meaning
String template "${var.name}-web" Insert a value into a string
Conditional var.prod ? "large" : "small" Choose between two values
For expression [for s in var.names : upper(s)] Transform a list into a new list
For expression (map) { for k, v in var.tags : k => upper(v) } Build a map
Splat aws_instance.web[*].id All the id values of a counted resource
Index var.names[0], var.tags["Name"] One element 
locals {
  upper_names = [for n in var.names : upper(n)]
  size        = var.environment == "prod" ? "large" : "small"
  all_ids     = aws_instance.web[*].id
}
Exam tip

. [for ...] builds a list; {for ...} builds a map; [*] is the splat. The conditional has three parts: condition, true value, false value.

2Functions

Terraform has built-in functions (and provider-defined functions from providers); you cannot write your own functions in HCL. You call them as name(arguments).

Category Examples
String upper, lower, format, join, split, replace, trimspace
Collection length, concat, merge, lookup, keys, values, flatten, element, contains
Numeric min, max, ceil, floor
Type conversion tolist, toset, tomap, tostring, tonumber
Filesystem file, templatefile, fileexists
Network cidrsubnet, cidrhost
Error handling try, can, coalesce

Use terraform console to try expressions and functions interactively against your configuration and state.

Exam tip

. merge combines maps, concat joins lists, lookup reads a map with a default, length counts. terraform console is the place to test an expression.

3count and for_each

Both create several instances of a resource or module from one block.

count for_each
Input A number A map or a set of strings
Instance index A number: aws_instance.web[0] A key: aws_instance.web["a"]
Inside the block count.index each.key, each.value
Removing an item May shift the numbers and replace other instances Only the removed key is affected
Use when Identical copies Copies that differ or stable names 
resource "aws_instance" "web" {
  count         = 3
  ami           = "ami-0abcdef1234567890"
  instance_type = "t3.micro"
  tags          = { Name = "web-${count.index}" }
}

resource "aws_s3_bucket" "logs" {
  for_each = toset(["app", "audit"])
  bucket   = "example-${each.key}"
}

count and for_each cannot be used together on one block.

Exam tip

. Prefer for_each when the items have identity, because removing one item does not renumber the rest. for_each needs a map or a set, not a list.

4Dynamic blocks

A dynamic block generates repeated nested blocks (for example several ingress rules) from a collection.

resource "aws_security_group" "web" {
  name = "web"

  dynamic "ingress" {
    for_each = var.ports
    content {
      from_port   = ingress.value
      to_port     = ingress.value
      protocol    = "tcp"
      cidr_blocks = ["10.0.0.0/16"]
    }
  }
}
Part Meaning
dynamic "ingress" The nested block type to repeat
for_each The collection to loop over
content The body of each generated block
ingress.value The current item (named after the block label)
Exam tip

. Use dynamic for repeated nested blocks inside a resource; use count or for_each for repeated resources.

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A team needs three identical virtual machines from one resource block. Which meta-argument is simplest?

  • Adynamic
  • Bdepends_on
  • Ccount
  • Dlifecycle
Show the answer

Answer: C. count creates a number of identical instances from one block.

S2A configuration creates a bucket for each name in a set of names. Which meta-argument fits and what is referenced inside?

  • Acount with count.index
  • Bdynamic with content.value
  • Cprovider with alias.name
  • Dfor_each with each.key
Show the answer

Answer: D. for_each creates one instance per element, and each.key and each.value refer to the current element.

S3Which expression returns a list with every name converted to upper case?

  • AA for expression in square brackets that applies upper to each name
  • BA for expression in curly braces that applies upper to each name
  • CA splat expression that reads an attribute called upper
  • DA function call that applies upper to the first name only
Show the answer

Answer: A. A for expression in square brackets builds a new list from the transformed elements; curly braces would build a map.

S4Which function combines two maps into one?

  • Amerge
  • Bconcat
  • Cflatten
  • Djoin
Show the answer

Answer: A. merge combines maps; concat joins lists.

S5A security group needs one ingress block for every port in a list that can change. What should be used?

  • AA count meta-argument on the nested block
  • BA data block per port
  • CA provider alias per port
  • DA dynamic block with for_each
Show the answer

Answer: D. A dynamic block generates repeated nested blocks from a collection.

S6Which command lets an engineer test an expression against the configuration and state interactively?

  • Aterraform fmt
  • Bterraform validate
  • Cterraform plan -test
  • Dterraform console
Show the answer

Answer: D. terraform console evaluates expressions and functions interactively.

5.2 Recall questions

R1What does the splat expression return?

Show the answer

The attribute from every instance of a counted resource.

R2Which function reads the length of a list?

Show the answer

length.

R3What inputs can for_each take?

Show the answer

A map or a set of strings.

R4Can count and for_each be used together?

Show the answer

No.

R5What does a dynamic block generate?

Show the answer

Repeated nested blocks.

R6Can you define your own function in HCL?

Show the answer

No; there are built-in and provider-defined functions.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Expressions template, conditional (condition ? a : b), for (list or map), splat, index
Functions built-in (and provider-defined): merge (maps), concat (lists), lookup, length, try; terraform console
count / for_each number / map or set; count.index / each.key and each.value; for_each is stable
dynamic repeated nested blocks: for_each plus content
